format: Pancho line ('say', max 15 words, plain English) + one block per step: kind D = formula toggle, A = labeled contrast cards, L = example list. [x] marks the part that changes. Max 2 steps, max 3 cards per step.

tips.title: Facturas
tips.dropped: The invoice meaning, kept only as 'not bills' in Pancho's line.

steps.say: At the bakery, facturas means pastries, not bills.
To order, just name it and add por favor.
Same again? Just otro. Never un otro.

opts: Otro café, por favor · Another coffee, please
Otra birra, por favor · Another beer, please

tips.title: Tostadas, un tostado
tips.dropped: 'Una tostada' as one slice at home.

steps.say: Tostadas is toast. Un tostado is a sandwich.

cards.en: A toasted ham and cheese, please.

tips.title: Un or una
tips.dropped: 'Agua is still an una word: otra agua'. Too early for that detail.

steps.say: Un or una goes with the thing. Learn it with each word.
One odd one: agua takes un.
¿Cómo andás? means how are you. Keep the answer short.
Che means hey. It goes first, with friends.
Soy means I am. You don't need yo.
The greeting changes with the time of day.
Short for all of them: buenas.

tips.title: De nada, joya
tips.dropped: 'Claro' (of course). It was a third idea; it can live in its own tip.

steps.say: When someone says gracias, answer de nada.
All good? Porteños say ¡joya!

tips.title: Soy, sos
tips.dropped: 'Use vos with everyone' moved to the vos tip right after.

steps.say: I am is soy. You are is sos.

tips.title: Vos
tips.dropped: The mention of tú. The course never uses it, so the tip doesn't either.

steps.say: In Argentina, you is vos. Use it with everyone, even your boss.
Surprised to see someone? Say ¿sos vos?
The ending matches the person: -o for him, -a for her.

tips.title: Disculpá, permiso
tips.dup: This tip is in unit 8 twice. Keep one.

steps.say: Disculpá gets attention. Permiso gets you past.

tips.title: Soy estudiante
tips.dropped: 'Vos can go before or after the verb'. That's already the ¿Sos vos? tip.
tips.dup: Two tips in unit 8 teach this same thing ('Soy estudiante, ¿sos turista?' and 'Soy turista — no un'). Keep one.

steps.say: Your role goes right after soy. No un.
Quick review: soy is me, sos is you.

opts: Soy Lucía, ¿y vos? · I'm Lucía, and you?

steps.say: Quick review: hi, bye and thanks.

tips.title: Me llamo, te llamás
tips.dup: This tip is in unit 10 twice, in two versions. Keep one.

steps.say: Me llamo is my name is. To ask: ¿cómo te llamás?

tips.title: Hablo, hablás
tips.dropped: The odd ones (sé, sabés). They come later, in their own tip.

steps.say: I ends in -o. Vos puts the stress at the end.

opts: Hablo un poco · I speak a little

steps.say: Me and te go before the verb.

tips.title: Ask for help
tips.dropped: 'Hablo un poco' (it's in Hablo, hablás) and 'castellano'.

steps.say: Stuck? These get you help.
